literal: Evil things oneself unto others let one not do, painful things oneself afflicting he who does not desire.
translation: Let a man not do evil to others, if he does not wish painful consequences to afflict him.
modern: துன்பம் தரும் செயல்கள் தன்னை வந்து தாக்குவதை விரும்பாதவன், தான் பிறருக்குத் தீமையான செயல்களைச் செய்யக்கூடாது.
explanation: This couplet warns against committing evil deeds by appealing to self-interest. The word 'தீப்பால' refers to actions that are evil by nature, while 'நோய்ப்பால' refers to the painful consequences that naturally follow. The poet states that if a person does not wish to be afflicted by suffering, he must refrain from doing evil to others. The underlying principle is that the harm one inflicts on others will inevitably return to cause pain to oneself.
